Insurance

Schengen Travel Insurance for Kenyans

Schengen visa applicants are generally asked to show medical travel insurance valid across the Schengen area for the whole stay, with minimum medical and repatriation cover. Requirements are set by the consulate and can change, so confirm them before you buy.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Emergency medical expenses and repatriation, usually with a minimum limit set by the visa rules
  • Validity across the Schengen area
  • Cover for the full period of stay

Who needs it

  • Kenyans applying for short-stay Schengen visas
  • Business travellers and students visiting Schengen countries

Common risks

A policy that does not meet the rules

A policy with the wrong dates, area or limit can cause problems with an application.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Visa decisions are made by the consulate, not the insurer.
  • Cover is subject to policy terms and exclusions.

What affects the premium

  • Trip length
  • Traveller age
  • Limit
  • Start and end dates

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Passport details
  • Travel dates and Schengen destination
  • Traveller date of birth
  • Consulate requirements, if you have them

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

What cover amount do I need?

Consulates have generally asked for a minimum medical cover amount and repatriation. Check the current requirement for your consulate. We can then match a policy to it.
